title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1LC1LD_---1LA_1LB1LE_0RF0RA_1LD1RF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1LC1LD_---1LA_1LB1LE_0RF0RA_1LD1RF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and probably cannot be settled by computation. Lean proves that the machine halts from blank tape exactly when an explicit arithmetic iteration reaches its halting case (halts_iff). The kernel evaluates its first epochs: they do not halt, and epoch 3 provably ends in a new epoch 4. Epoch 4 starts with a run of about 102·1013 ones; whether it halts at its end depends on parities of numbers with more than 1013 digits. Heuristically it halts there with probability 3/4, and eventually with probability 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 60,017 cells have been visited and 41,859 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496).

claims.title: One phase
claims.text: Write P c u x for the tape 0^inf 1^c (01)^u 0 0 (10)^x F> 0^inf. For u = 2 or 3 and x ≥ 1, P (c+4) u x reaches P c u' x' with X = x+u+4, u' = 2 + X mod 2, x' = 3⌊X/2⌋ − 1: four ones are eaten on the left, the block on the right grows by half. Built from the bounce rule L (01)^(x+2) 0 0 (10)^(y+1) F> → L (01)^x 0 0 (10)^(y+4) F> (4y+18 steps) applied k times.

claims.title: The eight epoch ends
claims.text: When fewer than 4 ones are left (r = c mod 4) and x ≥ 16: r = 3 gives the new epoch P (2x+4+2u) 3 5; r = 0 with u = 3, or r = 1 with u = 2, gives P (2x+5) 3 5; the four other cases (r = 0, u = 2; r = 1, u = 3; r = 2) halt.

claims.title: Halting is the iteration reaching none
claims.text: With epochs 0 = some 3 and epochs (k+1) = (epochs k).bind ends, where ends c applies c/4 phases to (u, x) = (3, 5) and then the epoch-end table: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if epochs k = none for some k.

claims.title: The first epochs
claims.text: epochs 1 = some 20, epochs 2 = some 297, epochs 3 = some 459271258863231 (evaluated by the kernel), and epochs 4 is defined because 459271258863231 mod 4 = 3. So the machine does not halt before the end of epoch 4.

claims.title: The model agrees with simulation
claims.text: An exact accelerated simulator (run-length tape, symbolic shift rules) matches the phase and epoch-end rules on the first 400 configurations of the form P, through epoch 3 (to about 10<sup>114</sup> steps), and on all eight epoch-end cases at x = 1000, 1001, 1002.

claims.title: It probably halts, unimaginably late
claims.text: Epoch 3 makes 114,817,814,715,807 phases, so c<sub>4</sub> = 2x+4+2u has about 2·10<sup>13</sup> digits and c<sub>4</sub> mod 4 = 2(x+u) mod 4. If x+u is odd, epoch 4 ends with r = 2: a halt. If it is even, epoch 4 halts unless its own last u is 3. With the parities behaving like coin flips, the halt comes at the end of epoch 4 with probability 3/4, and eventually with probability 1 (r = 3 is always followed by r = 0 or 2, and r = 2 always halts). Computing the parity needs about 10<sup>27</sup> bit operations at the very least.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known: equivalent (in Lean) to whether the epoch iteration ever reaches its halting case. The first undecided epoch end needs the parity of x+u after 1.1·10<sup>14</sup> steps of X → ⌊3X/2⌋+5, numbers of up to 10<sup>13</sup> digits; heuristically it halts there with probability 3/4.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, and the answer is hidden in a parity of a number with ten trillion digits. The machine eats a row of 1s four at a time while a block next to it grows by half each time, like the Hydra and Antihydra cryptids; when the row runs out, the remainder mod 4 decides whether it stops or starts again with a row whose length has trillions of digits.

facts.text: One phase: 4 ones eaten on the left, the block on the right grows by half (proved for all sizes).
Halting from blank tape is exactly the epoch iteration reaching its halting case.
The first epochs; none halts, and epoch 3 ends in a new epoch.
Chance that the end of epoch 4 is a halt.
No halt in the C simulator; 60,017 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Eat four, grow by half
html: Stop the machine whenever the head, in state F, stands just right of everything it has written. From step 139 on, the tape then always has the same shape:

call it P c u x; u is always 2 or 3. The head shuttles back and forth inside the right part: each trip moves two 01 pairs from the middle into three new 10 pairs on the right (the bounce rule). When the middle is used up, the head goes further left, bites 4 ones off the run on the left and rebuilds the middle. Altogether one phase is
P (c+4) u x   →   P c u' x'      X = x + u + 4,  u' = 2 + (X mod 2),  x' = 3·⌊X/2⌋ − 1

In terms of X alone this is X → ⌊3X/2⌋ + 5, the same kind of map that drives the famous cryptids Hydra and Antihydra. The block grows by half per phase, so the tape keeps growing to the right only, and the step count of a phase is about the square of its size.

sections.heading: When the ones run out
html: An epoch starts at P c 3 5 and makes ⌊c/4⌋ phases. Then fewer than 4 ones are left, r = c mod 4, and the parity hidden in u decides:

• r = 3: always a new epoch, P (2x+4+2u) 3 5;
  • r = 0: a new epoch P (2x+5) 3 5 if u = 3, a halt if u = 2;
  • r = 1: a new epoch P (2x+5) 3 5 if u = 2, a halt if u = 3;
  • r = 2: a halt.
The new run of ones is twice the block, so each epoch is exponentially longer than the one before. From blank tape:

epoch 0   P 3 3 5                   step 139      0 phases, r = 3
epoch 1   P 20 3 5                  step 364      5 phases, r = 0, u = 3
epoch 2   P 297 3 5                              74 phases, r = 1, u = 2
epoch 3   P 459271258863231 3 5     ~10^28 steps  1.1·10^14 phases, r = 3: safe
epoch 4   P c4 3 5, c4 with about 2·10^13 digits     r = 0 or 2: ?
All of this is proved in Lean: the theorem halts_iff says that the machine halts exactly when this iteration reaches a halting case, and the kernel computes the first four epochs.

sections.heading: Will it stop?
html: Epoch 3 ends safely because 459271258863231 leaves remainder 3 when divided by 4. Its end produces c4 = 2x+4+2u, so c4 mod 4 is 0 or 2 depending on whether x+u is even or odd after 114,817,814,715,807 phases. If it is 2, the machine halts at the end of epoch 4. If it is 0, it halts unless the last u of epoch 4 is 3.

Those parities depend on every digit of numbers that grow to about 1013 digits: computing even the first one is far beyond any computer. If they behave like fair coins, the machine halts at the end of epoch 4 with probability 3/4, after a number of steps that itself has about 102·1013 digits, and with probability 1 eventually. Unlike Antihydra, which is expected never to halt, this one is expected to halt, but its question looks just as hard to settle.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496).
After 109 steps the tape spans 60,017 cells (3 left of the start, 44,019 right), with a density of 1s of 0.697.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Hydra-like: each epoch eats a run of c ones 4 at a time while a block grows by X -> floor(3X/2)+5; c mod 4 and the last parity decide halt or a new, vastly longer epoch. Proved in Lean: halts iff this iteration reaches its halting case; epochs 0-3 computed, epoch 4 (c with ~2*10^13 digits) is out of reach and would halt at its end with heuristic chance 3/4.
